messages:
alex.k: quick heads-up — ran a perf + flamegraph on the CPU path for a 8k-batch streaming run. seeing a surprising ~28% time in Python during tokenization + scheduler path. attaching quick notes.

maria.p: nice, can you paste the perf command and the flame link?

alex.k: ran `perf record -F 99 -g -a -- sleep 60` while replaying traces; then `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > cpu-flame.svg`

alex.k: flame (internal): https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/tokenflow-1772248123.svg

alex.k: top of flame shows `tokenizer.py:tokenize_batch` -> `pybind::tokenize` (C++ bridge) -> `PyObject_Call` chain -> `sched.py:choose_batch` -> `batcher.py:should_flush`.

alex.k: raw perf topline: samples: total=463k; python_symbols ~130k (28.1%); kernel 14k; libc 40k; other C++ 90k.

sam.j: hmm 28% is big. is the tokenizer pure python? I thought we call into fast-tokenizer (rust/cpp)

alex.k: we do — but we still have heavy allocation/decoding in the Python wrapper. stack shows `PyUnicode_Decode` and `PyList_Append` a lot.

lee.t: maybe the glue is allocating per token. any hotspot in `realloc` or `memcpy`?

alex.k: yes `memcpy` and `malloc` spikes when batch size > 16. but smaller batches are fine. heuristic might be forcing eager concatenation.

maria.p: what about scheduler? you said `choose_batch` shows up — is it doing O(n^2) checks?

alex.k: choose_batch iterates `pending` and checks prefix cache hits to decide joinable groups. profiling shows ~9% in that loop; main cost is Python-level set/dict lookups (`__contains__`) and creating small tuples for keys.

sam.j: quick mitigation: try caching hashed keys (precompute in C++ layer) and expose an `is_joinable_fast` boolean to avoid allocations.

alex.k: agree. I'll prototype caching in C++ wrapper so scheduler receives ints instead of tuples. initial microbench: reduces scheduler CPU from 9% -> 2.5% in a 1k-sample run.

perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood.internal/traces/1772248123 (nsys + perf side-by-side)

lee.t: also consider a token-prefetch path: if KV-cache miss probability < 10% we can pre-allocate buffers and avoid per-token PyList ops.

maria.p: any regression compared to last week's baseline? CI perf baseline (1771600000) python% was ~12% overall IIRC.

alex.k: yep regression: baseline python% ~11.8 -> now 28.1. main delta caused by recent tokenizer refactor that added extra validation in Python layer.

sam.j: okay action items: 1) alex prototype C++ key-hash cache, 2) lee try prefetch path / buffer reuse, 3) maria add a perf unittest that records python symbol % and alerts >15% on main. i'll add jira tickets.

alex.k: posting small repro script here to run locally:

# replay harness (toy)
python3 replay.py --trace sample.trace --rate 500 --duration 60
perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pgrep -f replay.py) -- sleep 60
perf script | ~/FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
~/FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl out.folded > cpu.svg

alex.k: i'll push a branch with the C++ cache PR tomorrow, and attach new flame after.

maria.p: thanks — please tag `eng-runtime` PR and ping perf-bot on upload so we can track regressions :thumbsup:

sam.j: small note — also check `PyObject_Call` sites for unnecessary varargs tuples. flattening calls helped in another project.

lee.t: and add sampling with `perf record -g --call-graph dwarf` in case we miss inlined frames.

alex.k: noted. thanks team. we'll iterate and post follow-ups here.
